name: pii-redactor
description: A callable, offline Skill that detects personal data (PII) in inline text and returns a REDACTED copy for safe publishing, using only the Python standard library. Detects EMAIL, PHONE, CREDIT_CARD (Luhn-valid), SSN, IPv4, and best-effort NAME, replaces each match with a [REDACTED_<TYPE>] token, masks raw values in findings, and re-scans the output to verify zero residual matches. No network, no API keys.

files.description: Inline documents to scrub. Each item is an object with 'path' (label) and 'content' (the text to redact).

types.description: Optional subset of detectors to enable. Defaults to all six.

extra_names.description: Optional additional names to redact (matched case-insensitively as whole words).

compliance_notes: This Skill runs fully offline: it makes no network calls and reads no API keys or credentials.
All text is supplied inline (files[].content); the Skill does not fetch, scrape, or write files.
Findings never echo raw PII: each value is masked (e.g. 'j***@***.com', '4***'). Raw values are only removed from the content, never reported in full.
After redaction every detector is re-run on the output; redaction_verified is true only when zero residual matches remain.
NAME detection is intentionally high-recall / best-effort and can over- or under-redact; a human MUST review the output before relying on it.
This Skill provides redaction assistance, not legal advice; verify the redaction before relying on it to satisfy any privacy or compliance obligation.
Output is deterministic: no randomness, stable left-to-right ordering, and fixed [REDACTED_<TYPE>] tokens.
Errors are returned as a structured envelope with ok=false and an error.code; a Python traceback is never emitted.
